questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The annual range of temperature of Station X is
questions.explanation: Annual range = hottest month (31 °C in April and May) − coldest month (21 °C in January) = 10 °C.

questions.subject: Geography

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Station X is most probably located in the
questions.explanation: A single rainy season in the summer months, a long dry season and the hottest months just before the rains are typical of the tropical continental (Sudan savanna) climate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Station X lies in the
questions.explanation: The rains fall from May to September, the summer of the northern hemisphere, and January is the coolest month.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The number of months in which Station X receives less than 25 mm of rain is
questions.explanation: January, February, March, April, October, November and December each receive under 25 mm: seven dry months.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The mean annual temperature of Station X, to one decimal place, is
questions.explanation: Sum of the twelve monthly means = 319; 319 ÷ 12 = 26.6 °C.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The fall in temperature at Station X in July and August is best explained by
questions.B: cold ocean currents along the coast
questions.C: the sun being overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn
questions.D: heavy cloud cover and rainfall reducing insolation
questions.explanation: During the peak of the rains thick clouds cut down the sunshine reaching the ground, so the wettest months are cooler than the pre-rain months.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The ground distance from Ede village to Oba market is
questions.explanation: On a 1:50,000 map 1 cm represents 0.5 km, so 8 cm = 4 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The average gradient between Ede village and Oba market is
questions.explanation: Gradient = vertical interval ÷ horizontal equivalent = 200 m ÷ 4,000 m = 1 in 20.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The area of the forest reserve on the ground is
questions.explanation: 6 cm = 3 km and 4 cm = 2 km; area = 3 × 2 = 6 km².

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The river on the map flows towards the
questions.explanation: Contour V-shapes point upstream (towards the source), so with the Vs pointing north-east the river flows to the south-west.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The bearing of Oba market from Ede village is
questions.explanation: South-east is 135° measured clockwise from north; the back bearing from Oba to Ede would be 315°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Each grid square on the map represents an area of
questions.explanation: Grid lines 2 cm apart on a 1:50,000 map are 1 km apart on the ground, so each square is 1 km × 1 km = 1 km².

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: If the map extract is enlarged two times, its new scale will be
questions.explanation: Enlarging a map makes the representative fraction larger: 1:50,000 enlarged twice becomes 1:25,000.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A cross-profile is drawn from Ede to Oba with a vertical scale of 1 cm to 100 m. The vertical exaggeration of the profile is
questions.explanation: Vertical scale 1 cm to 100 m = 1:10,000; vertical exaggeration = horizontal scale denominator ÷ vertical scale denominator = 50,000 ÷ 10,000 = 5.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich, the local time at Town A is
questions.explanation: 15° of longitude = 1 hour; places east of Greenwich are ahead, so Town A is at 1 p.m.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich, the local time at Town B is
questions.explanation: 60° west = 4 hours behind Greenwich: 12 noon − 4 hours = 8 a.m. Monday.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When it is 12 noon at Greenwich, the local time at Town C is
questions.explanation: 120° east = 8 hours ahead: 12 noon + 8 hours = 8 p.m. Monday.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The time difference between Town B and Town C is
questions.explanation: Town B is 60°W and Town C is 120°E, a difference of 180° of longitude = 12 hours.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When it is 6 a.m. on Tuesday at Town C, the time at Town A is
questions.explanation: A is 105° west of C, that is 7 hours behind: 6 a.m. Tuesday − 7 hours = 11 p.m. on Monday.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: If the crop output of Alheri Farm is shown on a pie chart, the angle of the sector for cassava is
questions.explanation: Sector angle = share of total × 360°: 250 ÷ 600 × 360° = 150°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On the pie chart, the sector for yam would be
questions.explanation: Yam is 150 of the 600 tonnes: 150 ÷ 600 × 360° = 90°, a quarter of the circle.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The percentage of the farm's output that is rice is, to one decimal place,
questions.explanation: Rice is 100 tonnes out of 600: 100 ÷ 600 × 100 = 16.7% of the total output.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: If the output is drawn as a divided rectangle 12 cm long, the length of the maize portion is

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The most suitable diagram for comparing the output of the four crops side by side is a
questions.explanation: Discrete quantities for a few categories are best compared with bars of proportional length; the other three are maps of spatial distribution or movement.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The total annual rainfall of Station Y is

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The annual range of temperature of Station Y is
questions.explanation: Warmest months 21 °C (January and February) − coldest month 12 °C (July) = 9 °C.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Station Y lies in the
questions.explanation: January and February are the warmest months and June to August the coolest, so the station is south of the equator.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The climate of Station Y is best described as
questions.A: tropical monsoon (summer rain from the sea)
questions.B: equatorial (rain in every month of the year)
questions.explanation: Most of the rain falls in the cool winter months while the warm summer is almost dry: the classic Mediterranean regime of places such as Cape Town.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The rain of Station Y in June and July is mainly brought by
questions.B: convection currents in the summer heat
questions.C: the on-shore westerlies and their depressions
questions.explanation: In winter the belt of westerly winds shifts towards the equator, bringing cyclonic (frontal) rain to the western margins of continents in latitudes 30°–40°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A map on which 2 cm represents 1 km has a representative fraction of

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a map of scale 1:100,000, a road measuring 7.5 cm has a ground length of
questions.explanation: On 1:100,000 one centimetre represents 1 km, so 7.5 cm = 7.5 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A map of scale 1:50,000 is reduced to half its size. The new scale is
questions.explanation: Reducing a map makes each unit represent more ground: 1:50,000 halved becomes 1:100,000.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A farm measuring 3 cm by 2 cm on a map of scale 1:20,000 covers a ground area of

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The type of scale that remains correct even when the map is photographically enlarged or reduced is the
questions.explanation: A linear (graphic) scale is a drawn line that shrinks or grows with the map, so it stays true; a statement or RF becomes wrong.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A hill rises 250 m over a horizontal distance of 5 km. Its gradient is
questions.explanation: 250 m ÷ 5,000 m = 1 ÷ 20, written as 1 in 20.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Two points 6 cm apart on a 1:50,000 map lie on the 400 m and 100 m contours. The gradient between them is
questions.explanation: Horizontal equivalent = 6 × 0.5 km = 3,000 m; vertical interval = 300 m; 300 ÷ 3,000 = 1 in 10.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The bearing of a point due west of an observer is
questions.explanation: Bearings are measured clockwise from north: east 090°, south 180°, west 270°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: If the bearing of Kano from Zaria is 040°, the back bearing of Zaria from Kano is
questions.explanation: Back bearing = forward bearing + 180° when the forward bearing is less than 180°: 040° + 180° = 220°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A map drawn to a scale of 1:250,000 is enlarged five times. A river 4 cm long on the enlarged map is
questions.explanation: The enlarged scale is 1:50,000, on which 1 cm = 0.5 km; 4 cm = 2 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following scales is the largest?
questions.explanation: The smaller the denominator of the representative fraction, the larger the scale and the more detail the map shows.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The distance between two towns is 45 km. On a map of scale 1:300,000 they would be
questions.explanation: On 1:300,000 one centimetre = 3 km; 45 ÷ 3 = 15 cm.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The vertical distance between two successive contour lines on a map is called the
questions.explanation: The vertical interval is the height difference between adjacent contours, e.g. 50 m.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a 1:50,000 map the 500 m and 300 m contours are 2 cm apart on the western slope of a hill and 8 cm apart on the eastern slope. It follows that
questions.A: the western slope is steeper, with a gradient of 1 in 5
questions.B: the eastern slope is steeper, with a gradient of 1 in 5
questions.C: both slopes have the same gradient of 1 in 20
questions.D: the western slope has a gradient of 1 in 20
questions.explanation: West: 200 m over 1,000 m = 1 in 5; east: 200 m over 4,000 m = 1 in 20. Closer contours mean a steeper slope.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Contour lines that are very close together on a map indicate
questions.explanation: Closely spaced contours show that height changes rapidly over a short distance.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A series of contours forming closed concentric circles with the highest value in the centre represents a
questions.explanation: Values increasing inwards show rising land, that is a hill or knoll; a depression would have values decreasing inwards.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a contour map a spur is recognised by contours that
questions.A: form a V pointing towards higher ground
questions.B: form a closed circle with a hachured edge
questions.D: form a V or U pointing towards lower ground
questions.explanation: A spur is a tongue of high land projecting into lower ground, so its contours bulge towards the lowland; a valley's contours point upslope.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A low area between two hill tops, shown by contours that curve away from each other, is a
questions.explanation: A col (saddle or pass) is the gap between two summits and is often used by roads and footpaths.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A landform with a steep scarp slope on one side and a gentle dip slope on the other is
questions.explanation: An escarpment shows closely spaced contours on one side and widely spaced contours on the other.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A plateau appears on a contour map as
questions.A: widely spaced contours enclosed by closely spaced contours
questions.B: a single closed contour with a spot height in the centre
questions.C: a series of contours that cross and recross one another
questions.D: a V-shaped pattern of contours pointing downstream
questions.explanation: The flat top of a plateau has few contours, while its steep edges are shown by contours crowded together.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a human feature on a topographical map?
questions.explanation: Footpaths, roads, settlements and boundaries are man-made (cultural) features; spurs, cols and knolls are relief features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Two points on a map are said to be intervisible when
questions.A: they lie on the same contour line at the same height above sea level
questions.B: they are less than one kilometre apart on the ground
questions.C: a motorable road or footpath connects them directly
questions.D: no higher ground lies between them along the line of sight
questions.explanation: Intervisibility is tested by drawing a cross-section between the points; a convex slope or intervening hill blocks the view.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A convex slope is one that
questions.A: is steep at the top and gentle at the base
questions.D: is gentle at the top and steep at the base
questions.explanation: On a convex slope the contours are widely spaced near the summit and crowded near the foot; the summit cannot be seen from the base.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On a topographical map, the direction of flow of a river can be determined from
questions.A: the width of the blue river symbol drawn on the map
questions.B: the colour and thickness of the line used for the river
questions.C: the total number of tributaries joining the river
questions.D: the contours crossing the river, which V upstream
questions.explanation: Contours bend upstream when crossing a valley, and rivers flow from higher to lower contour values; tributaries also join at acute angles pointing downstream.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A settlement located at the point where a river becomes too shallow for ships is a
questions.explanation: Goods are transferred from water to land transport at the head of navigation, which encourages settlement growth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A topographical map shows a linear settlement along a road on a low ridge between two swamps. The best explanation of the pattern is
questions.A: the need for defence against attack
questions.D: avoidance of flood-prone land and access to the road
questions.explanation: Houses string out along the only dry, accessible strip of land; linear patterns commonly follow roads, rivers or dry ridges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Brown lines used on a topographical map to join places of equal height are called
questions.explanation: Contours are isolines of altitude; isobars join equal pressure, isohyets equal rainfall and isotherms equal temperature.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A trigonometrical station on a map indicates
questions.A: a point whose height and position were fixed by survey
questions.B: a junction where two or more railway lines meet
questions.C: the exact source of a river on a hill top
questions.D: a point where the compass suffers local attraction
questions.explanation: Trig points are accurately surveyed control points, usually on hill tops, marked with a triangle and a height.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The pattern of a river and its tributaries that resembles the branches of a tree is called
questions.explanation: Dendritic (tree-like) drainage develops on rocks of uniform resistance; trellis patterns follow alternating bands of hard and soft rock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Streams flowing outward in all directions from a central high point form a
questions.explanation: Radial drainage is typical of volcanic cones and dome-shaped uplands such as the Jos Plateau.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A map that uses shading of varying intensity to show population density by state is a
questions.explanation: Choropleth maps shade administrative areas according to the class of the value being mapped.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lines drawn on a map to join places with the same amount of rainfall are
questions.explanation: Isohyets show rainfall; isohels show sunshine; isobars pressure; isotherms temperature.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The volume of traffic moving between towns is best shown by a
questions.explanation: Flow lines follow the route and their width is proportional to the quantity moved.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A disadvantage of the dot map is that
questions.A: it cannot show the distribution of a phenomenon over an area
questions.B: it can only ever show the distribution of one crop at a time
questions.C: it requires the use of several colours and expensive printing
questions.D: dots may merge in dense areas making counting impossible
questions.explanation: Where values are high, dots coalesce into a black mass and individual dots can no longer be counted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main advantage of a pie chart is that it
questions.A: shows changes in a quantity over a long period of time clearly
questions.B: shows the exact location of each item on the ground
questions.C: can show negative values as well as positive ones on the same chart
questions.D: shows the proportion of each part to the whole at a glance
questions.explanation: The 360° circle represents the total and each sector is proportional to its share.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A country produced 40% of its electricity from gas. On a pie chart the gas sector would be
questions.explanation: A pie chart shares 360° in proportion: 40% of 360° = 0.4 × 360° = 144°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which diagram is most suitable for showing the monthly rainfall and temperature of a station on the same sheet?
questions.A: a combined bar graph (rainfall) and line graph (temperature)
questions.B: a dot map with one dot for every 10 mm of rainfall each month
questions.C: a flow-line map whose line widths show the monthly totals
questions.D: a choropleth map shaded according to the monthly totals
questions.explanation: The standard climograph plots rainfall as bars and temperature as a line against the twelve months.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Proportional circles on a map are used to show
questions.A: the direction of movement of goods
questions.B: the boundaries of local government areas
questions.D: quantities such as town populations at their locations
questions.explanation: The area of each circle is made proportional to the quantity it represents and it is drawn at the place concerned.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A student wishes to draw proportional circles for two towns with populations of 100,000 and 400,000. If the first circle has a radius of 1 cm, the second should have a radius of
questions.explanation: Circle area must be proportional to population, and area varies with the square of the radius: √4 × 1 cm = 2 cm.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A histogram differs from a simple bar graph in that a histogram
questions.A: uses proportional circles instead of bars to show the values
questions.B: is always drawn on a base map to show location
questions.C: can only show two values at a time on the same pair of axes
questions.D: shows continuous grouped data with bars touching one another
questions.explanation: Histograms plot frequency against continuous class intervals, so the bars are adjacent.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main weakness of a choropleth map is that it
questions.A: cannot make use of shading or colour to show different classes
questions.B: shows exact figures for every single point within each area
questions.C: cannot show more than two classes of value on the same map
questions.D: suggests that the value is uniform throughout each area shaded
questions.explanation: Shading an entire state one tone hides variations within it and creates abrupt changes at boundaries.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A multiple (compound) bar graph is used to
questions.A: show the routes followed by migrants moving between regions
questions.B: show the share of each part in a whole as sectors of a circle
questions.C: join all the places on a map that have the same value
questions.D: compare several variables for each of a number of years or places
questions.explanation: Grouped bars allow, for example, the output of three crops to be compared for each of five years.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The surveying method that measures distances only and fixes points by triangles is
questions.explanation: Chain (or tape) surveying builds a framework of well-conditioned triangles from linear measurements alone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In chain surveying, the short perpendicular distances measured from the chain line to details such as buildings are called
questions.explanation: Offsets locate features on either side of the chain line; tie lines fix distant details and check lines verify accuracy.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main line from which a chain survey framework is built is the
questions.explanation: The base line is the longest line, measured most carefully, usually through the middle of the area.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following instruments is used in chain surveying?
questions.explanation: Ranging poles, arrows, tapes, the chain, cross staff and field book are chain survey equipment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The arrows used in chain surveying are for
questions.A: marking the end of each chain length
questions.D: recording data in the field book
questions.explanation: Steel arrows (pins) are stuck into the ground at the end of every chain length so that the number of lengths can be counted.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The instrument used to set out a right angle from the chain line in chain surveying is the
questions.explanation: The cross staff (or optical square) is used to erect perpendicular offsets.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In prismatic compass surveying, a traverse that ends at the starting point is called
questions.explanation: Closed traverses return to the start, allowing the angular error to be checked and distributed.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The prismatic compass is used mainly to measure
questions.explanation: Bearings of survey lines are read through the prism against the graduated card of the compass.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The angle between true north and magnetic north at a place is called
questions.explanation: Magnetic declination (variation) differs from place to place and changes slowly with time.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A compass needle deflected by nearby iron objects or electric cables is said to suffer from
questions.explanation: Local attraction gives false bearings; it is detected when the forward and back bearings of a line do not differ by exactly 180°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In a compass traverse the forward bearing of line PQ is 070°. If there is no local attraction, the back bearing QP should be
questions.explanation: Back bearing = 070° + 180° = 250°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: An advantage of chain surveying is that
questions.A: it is suitable for large hilly areas
questions.D: the equipment is simple and cheap
questions.explanation: Chain surveying needs only a chain, tape, poles and arrows, but it is slow and unsuitable for large or rough terrain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A disadvantage of chain surveying is that it
questions.A: cannot be used on flat open land where there are no obstacles
questions.B: requires expensive electronic equipment and highly trained staff
questions.C: is unsuitable for large areas with thick vegetation or steep slopes
questions.D: cannot record any detail lying to the side of the chain line
questions.explanation: Obstacles, slopes and dense bush make chaining slow and inaccurate; compass or theodolite methods are then preferred.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The book in which measurements are recorded during a chain survey is the
questions.explanation: The field book has a central column for chainage with offsets recorded to left and right.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The bearings recorded at four stations of a closed compass traverse have a closing error. The error is normally
questions.A: ignored if it is less than 90°
questions.B: added to the first station only
questions.D: used to reduce the scale of the plan
questions.explanation: A small closing error is shared out over the traverse stations before plotting (Bowditch adjustment).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Geographic Information System (GIS) is best described as a
questions.A: hand-drawn map of a locality showing its roads, rivers and settlements
questions.B: satellite placed in orbit round the earth to photograph its surface
questions.C: magnetic compass used in surveying to measure the bearings of lines
questions.D: computer-based system for capturing, storing, analysing and displaying spatial data
questions.explanation: GIS links geographic locations to attribute data and allows map layers to be analysed together.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a component of GIS?
questions.explanation: GIS components are hardware, software, data, people (users) and methods (procedures).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Data that describe the characteristics of a feature, such as the name and population of a town, are called
questions.explanation: Attribute (non-spatial) data are linked to the spatial data that give the feature's location.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The GIS data model that represents the earth's surface as a grid of cells (pixels) is the
questions.explanation: Raster data, such as satellite images, store a value for each cell; vector data use points, lines and polygons.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Points, lines and polygons are the basic elements of
questions.explanation: Vector data represent wells as points, roads as lines and farms as polygons.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a source of data for GIS?
questions.explanation: Satellite and aerial images, GPS readings, existing maps, census reports and field surveys all supply GIS data.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The satellite-based system that gives the precise position of a receiver on the earth's surface is
questions.explanation: The Global Positioning System uses signals from a constellation of satellites to fix latitude, longitude and altitude.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The GIS technique of placing several thematic maps of the same area on top of one another to find relationships is called
questions.explanation: Overlaying, for example, soil, slope and rainfall layers helps to identify land suitable for a crop.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Converting a paper map into digital form by tracing its features is called
questions.explanation: Digitising creates vector data from analogue maps, either with a digitising tablet or on screen.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A planner wants to identify all houses within 500 m of a proposed refuse dump. The GIS operation required is
questions.explanation: Buffering creates a zone of specified distance around a feature so that objects inside it can be selected.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is an application of GIS?
questions.B: measuring rainfall with a rain gauge
questions.explanation: GIS is used in planning, transport routing, disaster management, resource mapping, health and agriculture.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: One major problem of using GIS in developing countries such as Nigeria is
questions.A: the absence of rivers and other natural features to map
questions.B: the absence of any satellites passing over the African continent
questions.C: the availability of too much accurate and up-to-date data
questions.D: the high cost of hardware, software and trained personnel
questions.explanation: Equipment, licences, reliable power and skilled staff are expensive and scarce, and base data are often outdated.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Remote sensing is the
questions.A: collection of information about objects without physical contact, usually from aircraft or satellites
questions.B: measurement of distances on the ground with a surveyor's chain and tape
questions.C: drawing of contour lines by hand from spot heights measured in the field
questions.D: recording of air temperature with thermometers kept in a Stevenson screen
questions.explanation: Sensors record reflected or emitted radiation, producing images used in GIS.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The planet nearest to the sun is
questions.explanation: The order from the sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The largest planet in the solar system is
questions.explanation: Jupiter's diameter is about eleven times that of the earth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The shape of the earth is best described as
questions.explanation: The earth bulges slightly at the equator and is flattened at the poles; its equatorial diameter (12,756 km) exceeds the polar diameter by about 43 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is evidence that the earth is spherical?
questions.A: the occurrence of earthquakes along the edges of the continents
questions.B: the existence of four seasons in the temperate regions of the world
questions.C: the circular shadow of the earth on the moon during a lunar eclipse
questions.D: the flow of all rivers from the highlands down to the sea
questions.explanation: Other proofs include circumnavigation, ships appearing hull-last over the horizon, the circular horizon and satellite photographs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The earth rotates on its axis once in
questions.explanation: Rotation from west to east takes 24 hours and causes day and night.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a result of the earth's rotation?
questions.B: varying lengths of day and night through the year
questions.C: the deflection of winds and ocean currents
questions.D: the overhead sun at the tropics
questions.explanation: Rotation causes day and night, the daily rising and setting of heavenly bodies, time differences and the Coriolis deflection; the seasons are due to revolution.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The seasons are caused by the
questions.A: rotation of the earth on its axis once every twenty-four hours from west to east
questions.B: changing distance between the earth and the sun as the earth moves along its orbit
questions.C: revolution of the earth round the sun with its axis inclined at 66½° to the orbital plane
questions.D: movement of warm and cold ocean currents across the surface of the oceans
questions.explanation: Because the tilted axis always points the same way, each hemisphere leans towards the sun for half the year.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The sun is vertically overhead at the Tropic of Cancer on
questions.explanation: 21 June is the summer solstice of the northern hemisphere; on 22 December the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: On the equinoxes (21 March and 23 September)
questions.A: the sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer
questions.B: the northern hemisphere has its longest day
questions.C: all places on earth have equal day and night
questions.D: the sun does not rise at the equator
questions.explanation: At the equinoxes the sun is overhead at the equator and the circle of illumination passes through both poles.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A place on longitude 45°E has a local time of 3 p.m. The Greenwich Mean Time is
questions.explanation: 45° east = 3 hours ahead of Greenwich, so GMT = 3 p.m. − 3 hours = 12 noon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The standard time of Nigeria is based on longitude
questions.explanation: Nigeria keeps West African Time, one hour ahead of GMT, based on the 15°E meridian.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The International Date Line roughly follows longitude
questions.explanation: A traveller crossing the line westwards gains a day and one crossing eastwards repeats a day; the line zigzags to avoid land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When it is 10 a.m. on Friday at a place on longitude 30°W, the time at a place on longitude 105°E is
questions.explanation: Difference = 135° = 9 hours; the eastern place is ahead: 10 a.m. + 9 hours = 7 p.m. Friday.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The great circle that divides the earth into the northern and southern hemispheres is the
questions.explanation: The equator (0° latitude) is the only parallel of latitude that is a great circle.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lines of longitude are also called
questions.explanation: Meridians run from pole to pole and are numbered east and west of Greenwich up to 180°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The angular distance of a place north or south of the equator is its
questions.explanation: Latitude is measured in degrees from 0° at the equator to 90° at the poles.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: At noon on 21 June the altitude of the sun at a place on latitude 40°N is
questions.explanation: The sun is overhead at 23½°N; the place is 16½° away, so the noon altitude = 90° − 16½° = 73½°.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Places within the Arctic Circle experience 24 hours of daylight on
questions.explanation: At the June solstice the whole area north of 66½°N is within the circle of illumination all day.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: An eclipse of the sun occurs when
questions.A: the earth comes between the sun and the moon
questions.C: the sun is overhead at the equator
questions.D: the moon comes between the sun and the earth
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse can happen only at new moon, when the moon's shadow falls on part of the earth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The layer of the atmosphere in which nearly all weather phenomena occur is the
questions.explanation: The troposphere holds most of the water vapour and dust; temperature falls with height until the tropopause.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The ozone layer, which absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation, is found in the
questions.explanation: Ozone is concentrated in the lower stratosphere between about 15 and 35 km.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The distance between the earth and the sun is approximately
questions.explanation: The mean earth–sun distance (one astronomical unit) is about 150 million kilometres; the moon is about 384,000 km away.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The outermost layer of the earth is the
questions.explanation: The crust (lithosphere) is thin, averaging about 35 km under continents and 5–10 km under oceans.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The continental crust is called sial because it is rich in
questions.explanation: Sial (granitic) rocks form the continents and float on the denser sima (silica and magnesium) beneath.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The core of the earth is believed to consist mainly of
questions.explanation: The core (barysphere or nife) is dense, hot and composed largely of iron and nickel.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rocks formed from the cooling and solidification of molten magma are called
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks are the primary rocks; they are crystalline and contain no fossils.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Granite is an example of
questions.explanation: Granite cools slowly deep in the crust, forming large crystals; basalt cools quickly at the surface and is fine-grained.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following rocks is formed from the remains of living organisms?
questions.explanation: Limestone, chalk and coal are organically formed sedimentary rocks; rock salt and gypsum are chemically formed.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When limestone is subjected to great heat and pressure it changes into
questions.explanation: Marble comes from limestone, quartzite from sandstone, slate from shale or clay, gneiss from granite and graphite from coal.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of sedimentary rocks?
questions.A: they occur in layers or strata and may contain fossils
questions.B: they are always crystalline and were formed from molten magma
questions.C: they never contain the fossils of plants or animals
questions.D: they are formed from lava that cooled quickly at the surface
questions.explanation: Sediments are deposited layer upon layer, often burying plant and animal remains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Coal is classified as
questions.explanation: Coal formed from compressed vegetation in ancient swamps.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which rock type is most likely to contain petroleum?
questions.B: basalt from a recent lava flow
questions.C: porous sedimentary rock such as sandstone
questions.explanation: Oil and gas accumulate in the pore spaces of sedimentary rocks trapped beneath impermeable layers, as in the Niger Delta.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Jos Plateau of Nigeria is made up mainly of
questions.B: sedimentary rocks of the Chad Basin
questions.explanation: The plateau's tin-bearing younger granites and old volcanic rocks give it its rugged relief and mineral wealth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following correctly pairs a rock with its mode of formation?
questions.explanation: Conglomerate is cemented pebbles; chalk is organic; basalt is extrusive (volcanic); quartzite is metamorphic.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rocks are important to man because they
questions.A: prevent rainfall from reaching the ground in dry regions
questions.B: cause earthquakes and volcanic eruptions along coastlines
questions.C: provide building materials, minerals and parent material for soils
questions.D: stop rivers from flowing into the sea during the dry season
questions.explanation: Granite and limestone are quarried for construction, ores are mined from rocks and weathered rock forms soil.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The rock cycle describes
questions.A: the movement of water between sea and land
questions.C: the movement of the earth round the sun
questions.D: the transformation of rocks from one type to another over time
questions.explanation: Igneous rocks weather into sediments, sediments become sedimentary rocks, and heat and pressure convert both into metamorphic rocks which may melt again.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The layer of the earth between the crust and the core is the
questions.explanation: The mantle (mesosphere) is about 2,900 km thick and its upper part is partly molten.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a metamorphic rock?
questions.explanation: Schist, gneiss, slate, marble and quartzite are metamorphic; shale and sandstone are sedimentary; basalt is igneous.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Molten rock beneath the earth's surface is called
questions.explanation: Magma becomes lava once it reaches the surface.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A large dome-shaped mass of intrusive igneous rock formed deep in the crust is a
questions.explanation: Batholiths are the largest intrusions and are exposed only after long erosion of the overlying rocks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A sheet of igneous rock that has solidified horizontally between layers of existing rock is a
questions.explanation: Sills lie parallel to the bedding planes; dykes cut vertically across them.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A dyke differs from a sill in that a dyke
questions.A: lies parallel to the bedding planes of the rock layers
questions.B: forms a saucer-shaped intrusion deep within the crust
questions.C: cuts across the rock layers vertically or steeply
questions.D: is always exposed at the surface as a flat-topped hill
questions.explanation: Dykes are wall-like intrusions filling vertical cracks; when exposed by erosion they form ridges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A volcano that has not erupted in historic times and is not expected to erupt again is described as
questions.explanation: Dormant volcanoes are sleeping and may erupt again; extinct ones are dead.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A volcanic cone built of alternate layers of lava and ash is called a
questions.explanation: Composite cones such as Mount Cameroon and Mount Kilimanjaro are steep and made of many layers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A large basin-shaped depression formed when the top of a volcano collapses or is blown off is a
questions.explanation: A caldera is much wider than a crater and may contain a lake, as at Lake Toba in Indonesia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A hot spring that periodically throws out jets of hot water and steam is a
questions.explanation: Geysers, such as Old Faithful in the USA, occur in volcanic regions where groundwater is superheated.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The point within the earth where an earthquake originates is the
questions.explanation: The focus (hypocentre) is underground; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above it.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The instrument used to record earthquake waves is the
questions.explanation: The seismograph records seismic waves; the Richter scale expresses their magnitude.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A giant sea wave generated by an undersea earthquake or volcanic eruption is called a
questions.explanation: Tsunamis travel across oceans at great speed and cause devastation on reaching shallow coasts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The only active volcano in West Africa is
questions.explanation: Mount Cameroon (about 4,040 m), close to Nigeria's south-eastern border, has erupted several times, including in 1999 and 2000.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Evidence of past volcanic activity in Nigeria is found on the
questions.explanation: Old volcanic cones, crater lakes and lava flows occur on the Biu and Jos plateaux and in the Mambilla area.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The concentration of volcanoes and earthquakes around the Pacific Ocean ('Ring of Fire') is best explained by
questions.A: the thinness of the ocean floor beneath the waters of the Pacific
questions.B: the strong ocean currents that circulate round the Pacific basin
questions.C: the great depth of the Pacific Ocean compared with the other oceans
questions.D: the presence of plate boundaries where crustal plates collide or slide past one another
questions.explanation: Most volcanic and seismic activity occurs along the margins of tectonic plates.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a benefit of volcanic activity?
questions.A: formation of fertile soils from weathered lava and ash
questions.B: destruction of settlements and farmland by lava flows
questions.C: generation of tsunamis by eruptions beneath the sea
questions.D: loss of life and property during violent eruptions
questions.explanation: Volcanic soils are rich in minerals; volcanic regions also provide geothermal energy, building stone and tourist attractions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lava that is very fluid spreads over a wide area to form a
questions.explanation: Basic lava flows far before solidifying, building extensive plateaux such as the Deccan of India.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The opening through which volcanic materials reach the surface is the
questions.explanation: Magma rises through the vent (pipe) and erupts at the crater.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The breaking down of rocks in place without removal is called
questions.explanation: Weathering disintegrates or decomposes rock in situ; erosion involves removal by moving agents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The peeling off of the outer layers of a rock owing to alternate heating and cooling is known as
questions.explanation: Exfoliation (onion weathering) is common in hot deserts and savannas with large daily temperature ranges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rainwater containing dissolved carbon dioxide dissolves limestone by the process of
questions.explanation: Weak carbonic acid converts calcium carbonate into soluble calcium bicarbonate, creating karst features.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The rusting of iron-bearing rocks, which turns them reddish-brown, is due to
questions.explanation: Oxygen dissolved in water combines with iron minerals to form oxides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Frost action as a form of weathering is most effective in
questions.explanation: Water in cracks expands by about 9% on freezing and shatters the rock where temperatures cross freezing point repeatedly.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The growth of plant roots in rock cracks is an example of
questions.explanation: Plants and burrowing animals break rocks physically, and decaying vegetation produces acids that decompose them.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The slow downhill movement of soil under the influence of gravity is called
questions.explanation: Soil creep is imperceptible but shows in tilted fences, poles and bent tree trunks.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the upper course of a river the dominant process is
questions.A: lateral erosion of the valley sides
questions.B: meandering across a wide flood plain
questions.C: deposition of alluvium on the flood plain
questions.explanation: Steep gradients give the young river energy to deepen its valley, forming V-shaped valleys, gorges and waterfalls.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: An ox-bow lake is formed when
questions.A: a river cuts through the neck of a meander and abandons the loop
questions.B: a river enters the sea and deposits its load in a wide estuary
questions.C: a dam is built across a river valley to hold back the water
questions.D: a glacier melts and leaves a hollow in the valley floor
questions.explanation: Deposition seals off the abandoned loop, leaving a crescent-shaped lake on the floodplain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A waterfall usually develops where
questions.A: a river flows over alternating hard and soft rock
questions.C: the river bed is uniformly soft
questions.D: a river flows across a flat plain
questions.explanation: The soft rock is eroded faster than the resistant band, leaving a step over which the river plunges.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Niger and Nile deltas are examples of
questions.explanation: Arcuate deltas are fan-shaped with many distributaries; the Mississippi has a bird's-foot delta.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: For a delta to form, a river must
questions.A: flow into a sea with strong tides and currents
questions.B: have a steep gradient at its mouth
questions.C: carry a heavy load into a calm sea or lake
questions.explanation: Sediment must be deposited faster than waves and currents can remove it; the Niger fulfils these conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The raised banks built along a river by repeated flooding and deposition are called
questions.explanation: Natural levees form because coarse sediment is dropped first when floodwater leaves the channel.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A crescent-shaped sand dune with its horns pointing downwind is a
questions.explanation: Barchans form where sand supply is limited and the wind blows steadily from one direction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A mushroom-shaped rock in a desert is produced mainly by
questions.A: wind abrasion, strongest near the ground
questions.B: river deposition during rare flash floods
questions.C: wave action along a former shoreline
questions.explanation: Sand carried by wind is concentrated in the lowest metre or so of air, undercutting the base of the rock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of wind deposition?
questions.explanation: Loess is fine wind-blown dust deposited far from its source; the other three are features of wind erosion.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A limestone region with sinkholes, caves and underground streams is described as
questions.explanation: Karst features develop where soluble limestone is dissolved along joints and bedding planes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Icicle-like deposits of calcium carbonate hanging from the roof of a limestone cave are called
questions.explanation: Stalactites hang from the ceiling; stalagmites grow up from the floor; the two may join to form a pillar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of marine erosion?
questions.explanation: Cliffs, caves, arches, stacks and stumps are erosional; spits, bars, tombolos and beaches are depositional.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A ridge of sand joining an island to the mainland is a
questions.explanation: Longshore drift builds the connecting ridge; a bar joins two headlands and may enclose a lagoon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Lagos lagoon was formed mainly by
questions.A: volcanic activity that created a large crater near the coast
questions.B: glacial erosion during the last ice age
questions.C: the deposition of a sand bar across a shallow coastal inlet
questions.D: the collapse of the roof of a large underground limestone cave
questions.explanation: Longshore drift built the sandy barrier beach that separates the lagoon from the Atlantic.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Agulu-Nanka gullies of Anambra State are a result of
questions.A: wind erosion of loose soils in a dry climate with little vegetation
questions.B: coastal wave action along a former shoreline of the Atlantic
questions.C: volcanic eruptions that split the ground into deep cracks
questions.D: severe gully erosion of loose sandy soils under heavy rainfall and deforestation
questions.explanation: Unconsolidated sands, steep slopes, torrential rain and removal of vegetation combine to produce gullies hundreds of metres wide.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A river that captures the headwaters of a neighbouring river through headward erosion produces
questions.A: an elbow of capture and a misfit stream
questions.B: a delta at the point of capture
questions.C: a levee along the captured river
questions.D: an ox-bow lake in the old valley
questions.explanation: The captured river's lower course is left too small for its valley (a misfit) and the sharp bend is the elbow of capture.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The process by which rock particles are removed and carried away by rivers, wind, ice and waves is
questions.explanation: Erosion involves detachment and transport; weathering only breaks the rock down in place.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The zone of a river where meanders, floodplains and ox-bow lakes are most common is the
questions.explanation: In the lower (old) course the gradient is gentle and lateral erosion and deposition dominate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A flat, low-lying area beside a river that is covered with water during floods is a
questions.explanation: Floodplains are built of alluvium deposited by successive floods and are usually very fertile.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Inselbergs found in the savanna regions of Nigeria, such as the Zuma Rock, are
questions.A: isolated residual hills left after long denudation of the surrounding plain
questions.B: volcanic plugs left when the softer cone around them was eroded
questions.C: coral reefs raised above sea level by movements of the crust
questions.D: sand dunes cemented into rock by lime-rich groundwater
questions.explanation: Inselbergs (island mountains) are steep-sided residual masses of resistant rock, commonly granite.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Chemical weathering is most rapid in the humid tropics because
questions.A: temperatures are low and the rocks contract and crack easily
questions.B: there is little vegetation to protect the rock surfaces
questions.C: high temperature and abundant moisture speed up chemical reactions
questions.D: frost action is common on the high mountains and plateaux
questions.explanation: Heat and water together accelerate solution, hydrolysis and oxidation, producing deep weathered layers.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The largest and deepest ocean is the
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about one-third of the earth's surface and contains the Mariana Trench.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The gently sloping submerged edge of a continent is called the
questions.explanation: The shelf is shallow (under 200 m), rich in fish and the site of offshore oil drilling.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a warm ocean current?
questions.explanation: The Guinea current flows eastwards along the West African coast; Benguela, Canaries and Labrador are cold currents.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The cold current that flows northward along the coast of Namibia and Angola is the
questions.explanation: The Benguela current cools the coast and contributes to the aridity of the Namib Desert.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Ocean currents are set in motion mainly by
questions.A: prevailing winds, differences in temperature and salinity, and the earth's rotation
questions.B: earthquakes and volcanic eruptions on the floor of the ocean
questions.C: the tides produced by the gravitational pull of the moon
questions.D: the discharge of large rivers such as the Amazon and the Congo
questions.explanation: Winds drag surface water, density differences drive deep circulation and the Coriolis force deflects the flow.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Warm ocean currents affect adjacent coasts by
questions.explanation: Winds crossing warm water pick up moisture; the North Atlantic Drift keeps north-west Europe mild and wet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Spring tides occur when
questions.A: the sun, moon and earth are in a straight line
questions.B: the sun and moon are at right angles to the earth
questions.C: the moon is at its first quarter
questions.explanation: At new and full moon the combined pull of sun and moon produces the highest high tides and lowest low tides.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Neap tides, the tides of smallest range, occur
questions.A: at new moon when the sun and moon are in line
questions.B: at full moon when the earth lies between sun and moon
questions.C: at the first and third quarters of the moon
questions.D: only in the tropics where the sun is overhead
questions.explanation: When sun and moon pull at right angles their effects partly cancel.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The average salinity of ocean water is about
questions.explanation: Salinity averages 35‰; it is higher in the Red Sea and lower near river mouths and melting ice.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Salinity is lowest in ocean waters
questions.A: near the mouths of large rivers and melting ice
questions.C: in enclosed seas such as the Red Sea
questions.D: in the doldrums with heavy evaporation
questions.explanation: Fresh water dilutes the sea, whereas high evaporation and low rainfall concentrate salts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lake Chad is an example of a lake formed in
questions.A: a shallow depression in a basin of inland drainage
questions.B: a volcanic crater on an extinct volcano
questions.C: a glaciated valley dammed by moraine
questions.D: an ox-bow cut off from a large river
questions.explanation: Lake Chad occupies a shallow basin fed by the Chari-Logone and has been shrinking through drought and abstraction.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lake Kainji in Nigeria is
questions.A: a crater lake on the Jos Plateau
questions.B: an ox-bow lake on the Benue flood plain
questions.C: a man-made lake behind a dam on the River Niger
questions.D: a lagoon separated from the sea by a sand bar
questions.explanation: Kainji Lake was created in 1968 for hydro-electric power, fishing and navigation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Lake Tanganyika, long, narrow and very deep, was formed by
questions.A: volcanic action that blocked a river valley
questions.B: river deposition across a shallow basin
questions.C: glacial erosion during the ice age
questions.D: faulting in the East African Rift Valley
questions.explanation: Rift valley (tectonic) lakes occupy troughs between parallel faults.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main sources of water in rivers are
questions.B: sea water pushed inland by the tides
questions.C: steam and water from volcanic vents
questions.D: moisture carried inland by dusty winds
questions.explanation: Rivers are fed by surface run-off, groundwater emerging as springs and, in cold regions, snow melt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The continuous movement of water between the oceans, atmosphere and land is the
questions.explanation: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, infiltration and run-off keep water circulating.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is an importance of oceans to man?
questions.A: they cause desertification along the coasts of the continents
questions.B: they prevent rainfall from falling on the land near the coast
questions.C: they moderate climate and provide fish, minerals, salt and transport routes
questions.D: they increase the speed of the earth's rotation on its axis
questions.explanation: Oceans are a source of food, oil and gas, sea salt, tidal energy and cheap bulk transport, and they regulate temperature.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The deepest part of the ocean floor is called
questions.explanation: The Mariana Trench in the Pacific descends to about 11,000 m.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Weather differs from climate in that weather is
questions.A: the condition of the atmosphere at a place over a short period
questions.B: the average atmospheric condition over about 35 years
questions.explanation: Weather describes the day-to-day state; climate is the long-term average of weather.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Atmospheric pressure is measured with a
questions.explanation: A mercury or aneroid barometer measures pressure in millibars; a barograph records it continuously.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The instrument used to measure wind speed is the
questions.explanation: The cup anemometer measures speed; the wind vane shows direction (the direction the wind blows from).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Relative humidity is measured with a
questions.explanation: The difference between the wet and dry bulb readings is converted to relative humidity using tables.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Thermometers at a weather station are kept in a Stevenson screen in order to
questions.A: protect them from direct sunlight and rain while allowing free air circulation
questions.B: keep them locked away from thieves and curious visitors to the station
questions.C: raise the temperature reading so that it matches the ground temperature
questions.D: measure rainfall and temperature at the same time with one instrument
questions.explanation: The white louvred box stands about 1.2 m above grass with its door facing away from the sun.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Six's thermometer is used to record
questions.A: the maximum and minimum temperatures of the day
questions.B: the atmospheric pressure at the time of reading
questions.C: the relative humidity of the air in the screen
questions.D: the number of hours of bright sunshine each day
questions.explanation: The U-shaped tube with two indices records both extremes since the last resetting.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The daily range of temperature is the difference between
questions.B: the maximum and minimum temperatures of a day
questions.explanation: Deserts have large daily ranges; equatorial regions have very small ones.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Temperature decreases with altitude at an average rate of about
questions.explanation: This normal (environmental) lapse rate explains why Jos and Obudu are cooler than the surrounding lowlands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A town at sea level has a temperature of 30 °C. Using the normal lapse rate of 6.5 °C per 1,000 m, the temperature at a town 2,000 m above sea level on the same day is about

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors is responsible for the small annual range of temperature at coastal stations like Lagos?
questions.B: the moderating influence of the sea
questions.explanation: Water heats and cools slowly, so the sea keeps coastal temperatures even; interior stations have larger ranges (continentality).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The belt of low pressure and calm, rising air near the equator is called the
questions.explanation: Intense heating makes air rise in the equatorial low; the sub-tropical highs are the horse latitudes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the northern hemisphere, the trade winds blow from the
questions.explanation: Winds blowing from the sub-tropical highs towards the equator are deflected to the right (Ferrel's law), giving north-east trades north of the equator.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Ferrel's law states that winds are deflected
questions.A: to the left in the northern hemisphere and to the right in the southern
questions.B: to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern
questions.C: towards the poles in both hemispheres because of the earth's rotation
questions.D: towards the equator in both hemispheres because of the earth's rotation
questions.explanation: The deflection (Coriolis effect) results from the earth's rotation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Harmattan is a
questions.A: warm moist wind from the Atlantic that brings heavy rain to the coast between June and September
questions.B: cool dry dusty wind from the Sahara blowing over West Africa between November and March
questions.C: monsoon wind from the Indian Ocean that brings summer rain to India and Bangladesh
questions.D: local sea breeze that blows onto the coast of West Africa during the afternoon
questions.explanation: The north-east trades pick up dust over the Sahara and bring haze, low humidity and cool nights.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A sea breeze blows
questions.A: from the land to the sea during the day
questions.B: from the sea to the land during the day
questions.C: from the sea to the land at night
questions.explanation: By day the land heats faster, air rises over it and cooler air moves in from the sea; at night the flow reverses as a land breeze.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rainfall that results from moist air being forced to rise over a mountain barrier is called
questions.explanation: The windward slope receives heavy rain while the leeward side lies in a rain shadow.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Afternoon thunderstorms in equatorial regions are typically produced by
questions.explanation: Intense surface heating causes strong convection, towering cumulonimbus clouds and heavy downpours.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Cyclonic (frontal) rainfall is produced when
questions.A: warm moist air rises over a cold air mass along a front
questions.C: air is heated from below by the ground
questions.D: air sinks in a high-pressure area
questions.explanation: It is common in temperate latitudes where tropical and polar air masses meet.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rainfall is measured with a
questions.explanation: The rain gauge is a funnel and bottle set in open ground, read daily in millimetres.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The temperature at which air becomes saturated and condensation begins is the
questions.explanation: Cooling below the dew point produces dew, fog, cloud or precipitation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The zone where the moist tropical maritime air from the Atlantic meets the dry tropical continental air from the Sahara over West Africa is called the
questions.A: polar front of the middle latitudes
questions.C: jet stream of the upper atmosphere
questions.D: trade wind belt of the sub-tropics
questions.explanation: The ITD (or ITCZ) migrates north in the northern summer, bringing rain to northern Nigeria, and retreats south in the dry season.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Nigeria's dry season is caused mainly by
questions.A: the southward shift of the ITD, allowing dry continental air to cover the country
questions.B: the northward shift of the ITD, bringing moist maritime air over the country
questions.C: the warm Guinea current flowing along the coast of the Gulf of Guinea
questions.D: heavy cloud cover that prevents the sun's rays from heating the ground
questions.explanation: When the ITD lies near the coast (December–February) the north-east trades (Harmattan) dominate most of the country.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The 'August break' in southern Nigeria refers to
questions.A: a public holiday declared at the end of the school year
questions.B: a short dry spell in the middle of the rainy season
questions.C: the onset of the Harmattan winds from the Sahara
questions.D: a period of severe flooding along the coast
questions.explanation: Rainfall in the south has two peaks (June/July and September) separated by the short August dry spell.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: High, wispy, feathery clouds made of ice crystals are
questions.explanation: Cirrus clouds occur above about 6,000 m and often herald a change of weather.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The cloud type associated with thunderstorms and heavy showers is
questions.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds tower to great heights with an anvil top.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the temperature of a place?
questions.explanation: Longitude affects time, not temperature; latitude, altitude, ocean currents, distance from the sea, cloud cover and aspect all affect temperature.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The sunshine recorder used at weather stations is the
questions.explanation: A glass sphere focuses the sun's rays and burns a trace on a card, showing hours of bright sunshine.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A weather station reports a wet-bulb reading equal to the dry-bulb reading. This means that
questions.explanation: No evaporation occurs from the wet bulb when the air is saturated, so both thermometers read the same.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The climate characterised by high temperatures throughout the year, a small annual range and heavy rainfall in all months is the
questions.explanation: Places such as Singapore, Douala and Warri have mean temperatures around 27 °C and over 2,000 mm of rain.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following Nigerian towns experiences a climate closest to the equatorial type?
questions.explanation: Calabar in the south-east has rain for most of the year, high humidity and a very small temperature range.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The tropical continental (Sudan) climate is characterised by
questions.A: rain throughout the year with two maxima and no real dry season
questions.B: a distinct wet season in summer and a long dry season in winter
questions.C: winter rainfall and summer drought with mild temperatures
questions.D: annual rainfall of less than 250 mm and a very large daily range
questions.explanation: Kano, Kaduna and Ouagadougou have this savanna climate, with the hottest months just before the rains.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Mediterranean climate is unique among world climates because
questions.A: it has rain in all seasons
questions.B: its rainfall comes mainly in the cool winter months
questions.C: it has the highest temperatures on earth
questions.D: it is found only in the southern hemisphere
questions.explanation: Summer drought and winter rain occur in the Mediterranean basin, California, central Chile, the Cape and southern Australia.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Hot deserts such as the Sahara are located
questions.B: on the western sides of continents between latitudes 15° and 30°
questions.C: on the eastern sides of continents near the poles
questions.D: along the Tropic of Cancer only in Asia
questions.explanation: Descending air of the sub-tropical highs, off-shore trade winds and cold currents keep these areas dry.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The tropical monsoon climate of India and Bangladesh is caused by
questions.A: the seasonal reversal of winds between land and sea
questions.explanation: In summer moist winds blow from the ocean onto the heated land; in winter dry winds blow from the land.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: In the Köppen classification, the letter A denotes
questions.A: dry climates in which evaporation exceeds precipitation
questions.B: tropical rainy climates with the coolest month above 18 °C
questions.C: polar climates with the warmest month below 10 °C
questions.D: warm temperate climates with mild winters above −3 °C
questions.explanation: A = tropical, B = dry, C = warm temperate, D = cold temperate (continental), E = polar.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A station records 2,500 mm of rain spread through the year, a mean annual temperature of 26 °C and an annual range of 3 °C. Its climate is
questions.explanation: Heavy year-round rain, constant heat and a tiny range are diagnostic of the equatorial climate.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The natural vegetation of the tropical continental climate is
questions.A: tropical rainforest with tall evergreen trees
questions.C: coniferous forest of pine and spruce
questions.D: Mediterranean scrub of olive and cork oak
questions.explanation: The long dry season prevents dense forest and favours tall grasses and fire-resistant trees.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Climates with very cold winters, warm summers and a large annual range of temperature, found in the interiors of North America and Eurasia, are described as
questions.explanation: Distance from the moderating sea gives interior stations such as Winnipeg an annual range exceeding 35 °C.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The Sahel region of West Africa has a
questions.A: semi-arid climate with short unreliable summer rains
questions.B: humid equatorial climate with rain in every month
questions.C: Mediterranean climate with wet winters and dry summers
questions.D: cold temperate climate with snow in winter
questions.explanation: Rainfall of 250–500 mm falls in a few summer months and varies greatly from year to year, making drought common.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of the equatorial climate?
questions.A: a large annual range of temperature
questions.B: double maxima of rainfall with no real dry season
questions.explanation: Rainfall peaks after each equinox when the overhead sun and the ITCZ pass over.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Cape Town, Perth, Santiago and Rome all share the same climate type because they are located
questions.B: on the western margins of continents in latitudes 30°–45°
questions.D: on the eastern margins near the tropics
questions.explanation: These western-margin locations lie under sub-tropical highs in summer and westerlies in winter, giving the Mediterranean regime.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main factor controlling the north–south variation of climate in Nigeria is
questions.A: altitude, which rises steadily from the coast to the far north
questions.B: distance from the Atlantic and the seasonal movement of the ITD
questions.C: longitude, since the country stretches across many meridians
questions.D: vegetation type, which changes from forest in the south to grassland
questions.explanation: Rainfall and its duration decrease from over 3,000 mm at the coast to under 600 mm in the far north.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The vegetation type with tall evergreen trees arranged in layers (storeys), lianas and epiphytes is the
questions.explanation: Dense canopy, buttress roots and great variety of species are typical of the rainforest of southern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Buttress roots are characteristic of trees in the
questions.explanation: Buttresses support tall trees rooted in shallow, heavily leached soils.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Mangrove trees are adapted to their environment by
questions.A: long tap roots that reach deep water
questions.B: stilt (prop) roots and breathing roots in tidal mud
questions.explanation: Mangroves grow in brackish tidal swamps, as in the Niger Delta and Lagos lagoons.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The savanna vegetation belt that covers the largest area of Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The Guinea savanna stretches across the middle belt from the forest edge to about 11°N.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a typical tree of the Sudan savanna?
questions.explanation: Baobab, shea butter, locust bean and acacia are drought-resistant savanna trees; iroko and mahogany are rainforest species.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Trees of the savanna are adapted to the long dry season by
questions.B: shedding their leaves and having thick fire-resistant bark
questions.C: growing in dense stands with closed canopies
questions.explanation: Deciduous habit, thick bark, small leaves, thorns and long roots reduce water loss and survive bush fires.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Plants adapted to very dry conditions, such as cacti, are called
questions.explanation: Xerophytes have thick fleshy stems, tiny or spiny leaves, waxy skins and long roots.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The temperate grasslands of North America, Argentina and South Africa are respectively called
questions.explanation: Prairies (N. America), pampas (Argentina), veld (S. Africa), downs (Australia) and steppes (Eurasia).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Coniferous (taiga) forests are characterised by
questions.A: broad-leaved evergreen trees such as mahogany and iroko
questions.B: needle-leaved softwood trees such as pine, spruce and fir
questions.C: thorny scrub and cacti adapted to long droughts
questions.D: tall grasses with scattered fire-resistant trees
questions.explanation: Conifers in Canada and Russia are the world's main source of softwood and paper pulp.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Mediterranean vegetation consists mainly of
questions.A: evergreen trees and shrubs with thick bark and small waxy leaves, such as olive and cork oak
questions.B: mangrove swamps with stilt roots growing in tidal mud along sheltered coasts
questions.C: tall elephant grass with scattered baobab and shea butter trees
questions.D: mosses, lichens and dwarf shrubs growing above the permafrost
questions.explanation: Plants must survive the hot dry summer, so they are drought-resistant (sclerophyllous).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The vegetation of the tundra consists mainly of
questions.A: tall hardwood trees with buttress roots
questions.explanation: Short cool summers and permafrost prevent tree growth in the Arctic tundra.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Montane vegetation is found in Nigeria on the
questions.C: Niger Delta and the coastal lowlands
questions.explanation: Cooler temperatures at altitude produce grassland and montane forest unlike the surrounding lowlands.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Much of the so-called 'derived savanna' of southern Nigeria was formed by
questions.A: climatic change alone, with no interference by man
questions.B: repeated clearing and burning of the original forest by man
questions.C: volcanic eruptions that buried the forest under ash
questions.D: a rise in sea level that flooded the coastal forest
questions.explanation: Farming, bush burning and logging have replaced forest with grassland along the northern edge of the forest belt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is an economic importance of the rainforest?
questions.A: production of timber such as mahogany, iroko and obeche
questions.B: grazing of large herds of cattle on open grassland
questions.C: production of dates and other fruits of the oases
questions.D: cultivation of wheat and barley on a large scale
questions.explanation: The forest also yields fruits, medicinal plants, rubber, and supports cocoa and oil palm cultivation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The factor that most determines the distribution of natural vegetation zones in West Africa is
questions.B: the amount and duration of rainfall
questions.explanation: Vegetation changes from swamp and rainforest in the wet south through savannas to semi-desert in the dry north.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Plants that grow on other plants without harming them, common in rainforests, are called
questions.explanation: Orchids and ferns perch on branches to reach light in the dense canopy.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Soil is best defined as
questions.A: any loose material lying on the surface of the earth, whether or not plants grow in it
questions.B: the thin upper layer of the crust, formed from weathered rock and organic matter, in which plants grow
questions.C: the solid unweathered rock that lies beneath the surface and supports the land
questions.D: the sand, gravel and mud found on the beds of rivers and along the coast
questions.explanation: Mineral particles, humus, water, air and living organisms are the constituents of soil.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The vertical section of soil from the surface to the parent rock is the
questions.explanation: The profile shows the horizons: A (topsoil), B (subsoil) and C (weathered parent material) above the bedrock.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The layer of soil richest in humus and most important for crops is the
questions.explanation: Organic matter accumulates at the surface, giving the topsoil its dark colour and fertility.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The washing down of soluble minerals from the topsoil to lower horizons by percolating rainwater is called
questions.explanation: Leaching is severe in the wet tropics and makes many rainforest soils poor in plant nutrients.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Laterite soils of the tropics are
questions.A: rich in humus and among the most fertile soils in the world
questions.B: red, rich in iron and aluminium oxides and often hard when dry
