questions.C: black in colour and full of lime from the underlying chalk
questions.D: found only in the hot deserts of the tropics and sub-tropics
questions.explanation: Heavy leaching removes silica and bases, leaving iron and aluminium sesquioxides; laterite is used for road building.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following factors influences soil formation?
questions.A: the colour of the sky and the phase of the moon
questions.B: parent rock, climate, relief, organisms and time
questions.C: the length of the rivers that drain the area
questions.D: the number of towns and villages in the area
questions.explanation: These five factors determine the type of soil that develops in a place.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Soil texture refers to the
questions.B: relative proportions of sand, silt and clay particles
questions.C: arrangement of soil particles into aggregates
questions.explanation: Loam, the best agricultural texture, contains a balanced mixture of the three sizes.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Clay soils differ from sandy soils in that clay soils
questions.A: drain very quickly and dry out soon after rain
questions.B: have large coarse particles with wide air spaces
questions.C: retain water and are sticky when wet and hard when dry
questions.D: cannot hold plant nutrients for any length of time
questions.explanation: The tiny clay particles pack closely, so drainage and aeration are poor but water and nutrient retention are high.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Alluvial soils are formed from
questions.explanation: Fertile alluvium on floodplains and deltas supports intensive farming, as on the Niger and Nile.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Chernozem (black earth) soils, among the most fertile in the world, are found in
questions.A: the equatorial rainforest of the Congo and Amazon basins
questions.B: the temperate grasslands of Ukraine and the Prairies
questions.C: the hot deserts of the Sahara and Arabia
questions.D: the tundra of northern Canada and Siberia
questions.explanation: Thick humus from decayed grass and limited leaching make chernozems ideal for wheat.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The removal of the soil layer by running water on a slope so that it is lost evenly over a wide area is called
questions.explanation: Sheet erosion is followed by rills (small channels) and then gullies as run-off concentrates.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following farming practices helps to conserve soil on slopes?
questions.A: ploughing up and down the slope
questions.explanation: Contour ridges and terraces slow run-off; strip cropping, cover crops, mulching and afforestation also protect the soil.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Crop rotation helps to maintain soil fertility because
questions.A: it increases the amount of rainfall received by the farm each year
questions.B: different crops use and return different nutrients, and legumes add nitrogen
questions.C: it removes all weeds and pests from the farm permanently
questions.D: it prevents wind erosion on the farm during the dry season
questions.explanation: Rotating cereals with legumes such as groundnut and cowpea restores nitrogen and breaks pest cycles.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The sequence of different soils found down a single hill slope, from crest to valley bottom, is called a
questions.explanation: Drainage and movement of material down the slope create a related series of soils (catena).

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Soils in the northern savanna of Nigeria are generally
questions.B: sandy, low in humus and easily eroded by wind
questions.C: deep black cotton soils rich in humus
questions.D: peaty and acidic with much organic matter
questions.explanation: Low rainfall, sparse vegetation and wind produce light sandy soils that need manure and irrigation for good yields.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Humus is important to soil because it
questions.A: makes the soil harder and more resistant to erosion by water
questions.B: supplies plant nutrients, improves structure and helps the soil hold water
questions.C: prevents weeds and other unwanted plants from growing in it
questions.D: removes all the air and water from the spaces between particles
questions.explanation: Decayed organic matter feeds soil organisms and binds particles into crumbs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Soil erosion is most severe in areas where
questions.A: vegetation cover has been removed on sloping land with heavy rainfall
questions.B: dense forest covers gentle slopes and protects the soil
questions.C: the land is perfectly flat and covered with thick grass
questions.D: rainfall is gentle and continuous throughout the year
questions.explanation: Bare soil, steep slopes and intense rain give maximum run-off and soil loss, as in south-eastern Nigeria.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Resources that can replace themselves naturally within a human lifetime are called
questions.explanation: Forests, fish, soil, water and solar energy are renewable if managed properly; coal and oil are not.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a non-renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels and mineral ores took millions of years to form and are exhausted by use.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is an atmospheric resource?
questions.explanation: The atmosphere supplies sunshine, wind, rain and the gases plants and animals need.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Water is regarded as a vital resource because it is used for
questions.A: domestic supply, irrigation, industry, power generation, fishing and transport
questions.B: making sedimentary rocks such as sandstone and limestone
questions.C: producing petroleum and natural gas in the Niger Delta
questions.D: causing earthquakes and volcanic eruptions along coastlines
questions.explanation: Dams such as Kainji combine hydro-electricity, irrigation, fishing and navigation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The importance of vegetation as a resource includes
questions.A: the provision of timber, fuel, food, medicine and protection of the soil
questions.B: the production of minerals such as tin, coal and iron ore
questions.C: the formation of igneous and metamorphic rocks in the crust
questions.D: the prevention of all rainfall over the areas that it covers
questions.explanation: Forests also regulate the water cycle, absorb carbon dioxide and support wildlife and tourism.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Land is a resource whose value to man depends on
questions.A: its distance from the equator only
questions.B: its fertility, relief, drainage, location and mineral content
questions.C: the number of rivers flowing into the sea
questions.explanation: These qualities decide whether land is used for farming, building, mining or recreation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The interaction between man and his environment is illustrated by
questions.A: man clearing forest for farming and the resulting soil erosion
questions.B: the orbit of the moon round the earth once every month
questions.C: the movement of warm and cold ocean currents across the Atlantic
questions.D: the eruption of Mount Cameroon and the lava flows it produced
questions.explanation: Human activities modify the environment, which in turn affects man; the other options are natural events independent of human action.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The concept of sustainable development requires that
questions.A: resources are used as quickly as possible so that the economy grows fast
questions.B: present needs are met without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs
questions.C: all mining and logging is stopped so that resources remain untouched
questions.D: only renewable resources are ever used and all others are left in the ground
questions.explanation: Sustainability balances economic growth with conservation of resources and the environment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following best explains why the Niger Delta is Nigeria's main source of petroleum?
questions.A: its thick volcanic rocks formed from recent lava flows
questions.B: its thick sequence of sedimentary rocks with suitable traps
questions.C: its high altitude above the level of the surrounding plains
questions.D: its granite basement rocks of great age
questions.explanation: Organic-rich sediments deposited by the Niger over millions of years generated and trapped oil and gas.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Environmental balance (ecological balance) refers to
questions.A: the equal size of all the countries that share an environment
questions.B: a state of equilibrium among living things and their environment
questions.C: a balanced government budget for environmental projects
questions.D: the balance of trade between a country and its neighbours
questions.explanation: Over-exploitation of one component, such as forest, upsets the balance and leads to problems such as erosion and loss of wildlife.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Solar energy is described as a renewable resource because it
questions.A: is very expensive to collect and store
questions.B: is continuously supplied by the sun
questions.C: is found underground in porous rocks
questions.D: is stored in coal and petroleum deposits
questions.explanation: Sunshine is inexhaustible on a human time scale and Nigeria receives abundant solar radiation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The spread of desert-like conditions into formerly productive semi-arid land is called
questions.explanation: Over-grazing, felling of trees for fuel, over-cultivation and drought are turning parts of Nigeria's Sahel into desert.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following Nigerian states is most threatened by desertification?
questions.explanation: The frontline states of the far north (Yobe, Borno, Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto, Kebbi, Zamfara, Kano and Bauchi) face advancing desert conditions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main cause of the rapid shrinking of Lake Chad is
questions.A: earthquakes in the basin that opened cracks in the lake floor
questions.B: prolonged drought and excessive abstraction of water for irrigation
questions.C: volcanic eruptions that filled the lake with lava and ash
questions.D: a rise in sea level that drained the lake towards the coast
questions.explanation: The lake has lost about 90% of its area since the 1960s, affecting fishing and farming communities.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Gully erosion in south-eastern Nigeria is worsened by
questions.A: the planting of cover crops and grasses on the slopes of the hills
questions.B: heavy rainfall on loose sandy soils cleared of vegetation and poorly planned drainage
questions.C: the flatness of the land, which makes run-off collect in pools
questions.D: irrigation farming on the flood plains of the rivers during the dry season
questions.explanation: Unchannelled run-off from roads and roofs concentrates into torrents that cut deep gullies.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The enhanced greenhouse effect and global warming are mainly caused by
questions.A: increased emission of carbon dioxide and other gases from burning fossil fuels and deforestation
questions.B: the eruption of volcanoes, which throw large amounts of ash into the atmosphere
questions.C: the rotation of the earth on its axis, which brings each place under the sun daily
questions.D: the depletion of iron ore and other mineral deposits through mining
questions.explanation: Greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat; consequences include rising sea levels, floods and droughts.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The depletion of the ozone layer is caused chiefly by
questions.A: carbon dioxide released by the burning of fossil fuels
questions.C: water vapour evaporated from the surface of the oceans
questions.D: nitrogen released by the decay of plants and animals
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine which destroys ozone, allowing more harmful ultraviolet radiation to reach the earth.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Acid rain results from
questions.A: the emission of sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides into the atmosphere
questions.B: excess rainfall in the tropics falling on soils that are already acidic
questions.C: the evaporation of sea water containing dissolved salts and acids
questions.D: the melting of glaciers and ice caps in the polar regions
questions.explanation: The gases dissolve in cloud droplets to form sulphuric and nitric acids that damage forests, lakes and buildings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Oil spillage in the Niger Delta has resulted in
questions.A: increased fish catches in the creeks and rivers of the region
questions.B: destruction of farmland, fisheries and mangroves and pollution of drinking water
questions.C: the formation of new fertile soils on the flood plains of the delta
questions.D: reduced rainfall and longer dry seasons over the whole region
questions.explanation: Spills from pipelines, wells and sabotage have devastated livelihoods in communities such as Ogoniland.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Flooding of the Niger and Benue valleys is worsened by
questions.A: the construction of dams downstream, which holds back the water in the lower valley
questions.B: heavy rainfall combined with the release of water from upstream dams and building on floodplains
questions.C: the Harmattan, which brings dust that blocks the channels of the rivers
questions.D: the planting of trees on river banks, which slows down the flow of water
questions.explanation: The 2012 and 2022 floods followed prolonged rain and releases from dams such as Lagdo in Cameroon.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Gas flaring in the oil-producing areas of Nigeria contributes to
questions.A: cooler temperatures in the surrounding villages
questions.B: air pollution, acid rain and global warming
questions.C: improved soil fertility on nearby farmland
questions.D: increased rainfall over the whole Niger Delta
questions.explanation: Burning associated gas releases carbon dioxide, soot and sulphur compounds and wastes a valuable resource.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The planting of trees on land that was previously bare or deforested is called
questions.explanation: Afforestation, such as the Great Green Wall project, checks erosion and desert encroachment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a measure for controlling soil erosion?
questions.A: bush burning before the start of the planting season
questions.B: construction of check dams and planting of cover crops
questions.C: clearing all vegetation from the slopes of hills
questions.D: overgrazing of pasture land by large herds of cattle
questions.explanation: Check dams slow run-off in gullies while cover crops shield the soil from raindrop impact.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The main purpose of national parks such as Yankari and Kainji Lake is to
questions.A: provide farmland for settlers from the crowded towns
questions.B: conserve wildlife and natural vegetation and promote tourism
questions.C: mine minerals such as tin and columbite
questions.D: generate hydro-electric power for the national grid
questions.explanation: Game reserves protect endangered animals and their habitats and earn revenue from visitors.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: An Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) is
questions.A: a study of the likely effects of a proposed project on the environment before it is carried out
questions.B: a report on the profit made by a company from the sale of its products
questions.C: a census of the wild animals living in a game reserve or national park
questions.D: a map of a national park showing its roads, camps and boundaries
questions.explanation: EIA law in Nigeria requires large projects such as dams, refineries and highways to be assessed before approval.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of deforestation in Nigeria?
questions.A: afforestation programmes carried out by the state governments
questions.B: logging, farming, fuelwood collection and urban expansion
questions.C: the creation of forest reserves by the federal government
questions.D: the strict enforcement of forestry laws by forest guards
questions.explanation: Nigeria has lost most of its original forest cover, leading to erosion, loss of biodiversity and climate change.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The removal of vegetation cover leads to increased flooding because
questions.A: rain no longer falls on the area and the rivers dry up completely
questions.B: infiltration is reduced and surface run-off reaches rivers more quickly

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Recycling of waste materials such as paper, glass and metals helps the environment by
questions.A: increasing the demand for raw materials from mines and forests
questions.B: reducing the volume of refuse and conserving resources and energy
questions.C: increasing the pollution of rivers and streams near the towns
questions.D: reducing employment in the factories that make new products
questions.explanation: Recycling lessens mining and logging pressure and cuts landfill and littering problems in cities such as Lagos.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Over-grazing in the Sahel contributes to desertification because
questions.A: the animals bring rain-bearing clouds with them as they move
questions.B: it removes the grass cover, exposing the soil to wind and water erosion
questions.C: it adds too much manure to the soil and makes it too fertile
questions.D: the cattle dig wells that lower the water table in the area
questions.explanation: Trampling and removal of vegetation leave loose soil that is blown away in the dry season.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Which of the following is a consequence of drought in northern Nigeria?
questions.A: increased crop yields because of the extra sunshine
questions.B: crop failure, death of livestock and migration of people southwards
questions.C: expansion of Lake Chad over the surrounding plains
questions.D: reduced Harmattan dust because the air is drier
questions.explanation: Drought years in the 1970s and 1980s caused famine and pushed Fulani herders into the middle belt.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Environmental conservation means
questions.A: using natural resources as wastefully as possible while they last
questions.B: the wise use and protection of natural resources for present and future generations
questions.C: banning all economic activities that make use of natural resources
questions.D: the study of maps and diagrams showing the distribution of resources
questions.explanation: Conservation includes afforestation, soil protection, pollution control, recycling and protected areas.
